items.title: RED: audit current primitives and reproduce only remaining Story 3 contract failures
items.context: First audit and characterize existing per-Story Finding locks, main/B-META locks, process-event append locks, build locks, Store atomic replacement, and current execution receipts. Preserve already-correct behavior as passing baseline evidence. For each still-missing Section 9.3 contract, add an executable RED that fails for the demonstrated reason, including as applicable unique durable allocation, idempotent replay, exact-record CAS, durable crash boundary, artifact/source binding, or runtime freshness. Bind every RED result to the pre-fix source hash; do not assert a historical race that current serialization already prevents.

items.title: Implement Story 3A fenced exactly-once Finding ledger writes
items.context: Audit and reuse existing per-story and B-META lock paths. Add collision-resistant monotonic or otherwise unique append-only record IDs independent of mutable array length, per-story fenced writer discipline, persisted ledger schema epoch and minimum writer capability, idempotency keys, and durable atomic temp-write plus file/directory fsync plus rename with explicit supported-local-filesystem and recovery boundaries. Idempotent retry returns the original record and receipt IDs through the idempotency receipt; record-ID generation itself must not become semantic identity or import Story 2 policy.

items.title: Implement exact-record CAS and signed FindingLedgerReceipt consumers
items.context: Implement the accepted FindingLedgerReceipt contract: schemaVersion, ledgerSchemaEpoch, minimumWriterCapability, receiptId, storyId, idempotencyKey, operation, recordIds, casBindings with expected record ID/hash and observed chain head ID/hash plus predicateDigest, priorLedgerDigest, committedLedgerDigest, replayed, committedAt, writer session/lease/fence token, trust fields, receiptHash, and signature. Later schema-neutral consumers must compare the exact referenced persisted record bytes and current chain state under the same fenced transaction; conflict writes no semantic records and idempotent replay returns the original record and receipt IDs.

items.title: Implement content-addressed RuntimeEvidenceReceipt and artifact stability checks
items.context: Implement the exact Section 6 RuntimeEvidenceReceipt signer/verifier and build-execution adapter, binding storyId, source HEAD/material, build policy and build/execution command digests, content-addressed command/stdout/stderr/environment/artifact-manifest blobs, redacted allowlisted environment with excluded names and policy digest, artifact path/digest/sourceHead and realpath policy, timestamps, exit and output digests, toolchain, command canonicalization, producer, key/algorithm/trust-root/key-freshness fields, receipt hash and signature. Refuse build-in-progress, unsupported trust or storage assumptions, tamper, stale source/artifact/environment/command, and artifacts that mutate before, during, or after execution via a post-run stability check.

items.title: Register Story 3 process facts and expose a protected read-only ledger query contract
items.context: Register atomic persistence and gate-eligible runtime evidence in the process-fact registry and contract verifier without granting persisted candidate, route, baseline, historical, or receipt bytes semantic gate authority. Expose a stable read-only query contract for ledger, CAS, idempotency, runtime scorecard, and migration inputs; return signed row digests and deterministic refusal reasons while never exposing protected storage paths. Add registry, command-policy, phase-allowlist, forbidden-import, direct-consumer, and non-authority mutation tests.

items.title: GREEN: prove ledger atomicity and runtime freshness contracts
items.context: Turn every genuine RED case GREEN, preserve audit-characterized existing behavior, and add adversarial concurrency, 100 unique appends plus replay, mixed-record transactions, legacy binding, exact CAS conflict, revoke-versus-apply serialization, crash recovery, migration, signature and trust, hash drift, artifact mutation, non-authority, no-nested-lock-deadlock, dependency-boundary, deterministic scorecard, protected query, rollback, and kill-switch verification evidence.
